hints: Focus on what actually changes in the atom as proton number rises across Period 3 while electrons fill the same outer shell.
Statement 1 is true because proton number rises from 11 to 17, so nuclear charge increases steadily across the period.

Check ionic sizes carefully, cations like $\text{Na}^{+}$ to $\text{Si}^{4+}$ are tiny but anions like $\text{P}^{3-}$ to $\text{Cl}^{-}$ jump much larger, and remember inner shell shielding stays almost constant.
walkthrough:
**Think about nuclear charge across the period**

Going from Na to Cl, each step adds one proton to the nucleus and one electron to the same n = 3 shell. So nuclear charge increases steadily.

$$\text{proton number: } 11 (\text{Na}) \to 17 (\text{Cl})$$

**Decide on statement 1**

More protons means a stronger pull on the same shell of electrons, so atomic radius decreases. Statement 1 is correct and explains the trend.

**Test statement 2 about ionic radius**

The most common ions are $\text{Na}^{+}$, $\text{Mg}^{2+}$, $\text{Al}^{3+}$, $\text{Si}^{4+}$, $\text{P}^{3-}$, $\text{S}^{2-}$, $\text{Cl}^{-}$. Radius falls for the cations, then jumps up hugely for the anions because an extra shell is now occupied.

$$\text{Na}^{+} > \text{Mg}^{2+} > \text{Al}^{3+} > \text{Si}^{4+} \text{ then jump to } \text{P}^{3-} > \text{S}^{2-} > \text{Cl}^{-}$$

**Test statement 3 about shielding**

Shielding is mainly caused by inner complete shells (1s, 2s, 2p). These do not change across Period 3, so shielding stays roughly constant, it does not decrease. The increased pull is due to higher nuclear charge, not less shielding. So statement 3 is incorrect.

**Conclude the correct combination**

Only statement 1 is correct. That matches the option for 1 only.

options.A: Incorrect because it claims all three statements are correct. Statements 2 and 3 are both false, ionic radius does not fall smoothly and shielding does not decrease.
options.B: Incorrect because it includes statement 2. Ionic radius falls from $\text{Na}^{+}$ to $\text{Si}^{4+}$ but then jumps up at phosphorus to form large anions, so there is no steady decrease.
options.C: Incorrect because it includes statements 2 and 3 but omits the true statement 1. Both 2 and 3 describe trends that do not happen across Period 3.
options.D: Correct because only statement 1 is true. Nuclear charge increases from Na to Cl, increasing effective nuclear charge and pulling electrons closer, while shielding stays about the same and ionic radius shows a jump between cations and anions.
